soil-fert-191.q: What does a soil nitrate test reading above the optimal range tell a corn grower?
soil-fert-191.a: Adding more nitrogen will not increase yield.

soil-fert-099.q: If nitrogen gas is the largest nitrogen store, why is usable nitrogen scarce in many ecosystems?
soil-fert-099.a: Little of the atmosphere's nitrogen gas is available to living things.

soil-fert-121.q: Why can ploughing in straw leave a crop short of nitrogen?
soil-fert-121.a: High-carbon straw stimulates microbes, which raise their nitrogen demand and out-compete the crop for ammonium and nitrate.

soil-fert-113.q: Which two groups of nitrifying bacteria work together, and what does each make?
soil-fert-113.a: Ammonia-oxidizing bacteria make nitrite, and nitrite-oxidizing bacteria turn it into nitrate.

soil-fert-143.q: Why is iron a limiting nutrient in most regions despite being abundant in the crust?
soil-fert-143.a: Where oxygen is present iron takes the stable ferric form, which dissolves poorly.

soil-fert-123.q: How does a build-up of ammonium in farm soil make it more acid?
soil-fert-123.a: Nitrification of the ammonium releases hydrogen ions that acidify the soil.

soil-fert-141.q: What separates a reservoir from an exchange pool in an element cycle?
soil-fert-141.a: A reservoir, generally abiotic, holds a chemical for a long time, while an exchange pool, generally biotic, holds it only briefly.

soil-fert-115.q: Why might ammonia-oxidizing archaea contribute more to ammonia oxidation in soils than bacteria do?
soil-fert-115.a: They outnumber ammonia-oxidizing bacteria in soils.

soil-fert-148.q: What gives salt marshes and mud flats their rotten-egg smell?
soil-fert-148.a: Hydrogen sulfide expelled by sulfate-reducing microorganisms.

soil-fert-130.q: What can soil phosphatase activity indicate?
soil-fert-130.a: The soil's potential for phosphorus mineralization and its phosphorus availability.

soil-fert-126.q: Why does the final microbial step to nitrogen gas matter for reactive nitrogen?
soil-fert-126.a: The atmosphere is the ultimate sink for reactive nitrogen, and denitrification returns it there as nitrogen gas.

soil-fert-110.q: What is unusual about the comammox Nitrospira found in 2015?
soil-fert-110.a: A single organism carries out complete nitrification, where two groups were long thought necessary.

soil-fert-001.q: Why do legumes generally need no nitrogen fertilizer?

soil-fert-050.q: What lets biochar serve for carbon removal?
soil-fert-050.a: Its refractory stability lets it persist in soils for thousands of years.

soil-fert-004.q: How does a compound NPK fertilizer differ from an NPK blend?
soil-fert-004.a: A compound binds the three nutrients chemically, while a blend is a physical mixture of single-nutrient fertilizers.

soil-fert-023.q: What did the once-common term artificial manure mean?
soil-fert-023.a: What are now called artificial fertilizers.

soil-fert-055.q: Where does the acidity of most acid soils generally come from?
soil-fert-055.a: From aluminium hydrolysis, since most acid soils are saturated with aluminium rather than hydrogen ions.

soil-fert-029.a: Aerobic bacteria need oxygen above 5%, so turning keeps up oxygen and the right moisture.

soil-fert-071.q: Why is ammonium nitrate a greater security risk than urea?
soil-fert-071.a: It forms explosive mixtures with fuels, while urea is not an oxidizer.

soil-fert-048.q: Can biofertilizers replace synthetic fertilizers today?
soil-fert-048.a: Not yet; they can reduce the use of synthetic fertilizers and pesticides but cannot yet replace them.
